My plant culture experiment so far (x-post botany)

Always a fun experiment. Baby food jars make good conatiners, you just need new lids. PlantTC.com has some good stuff in resonable quantities. I got kits from them and had a portion of my bedroom closet As a lab with hundreds of jars going at once.

Cheers!
I'll check them out. Been hitting some bumps in the road.

Made a separate post about it but basically my agar isn't gelling. Also not getting callus induction but I haven't been able to assess the variables on that issue (likely due to innacuracies and inexperience).

Sounds like your ratios are off. Making agar is just like jello, too much liquid and it won't set. Callus induction is largely a function of murk location hormone, maybe yours was too old or diluted. There are methods of using non gelled medium that I think do better as the solution surrounding the plantlet can get depleted in gel, in liiquid you just give it a swirl every so often. You need a physical support structure for the plantlet tho, I have used a kitchen plastic pot scubber, synthetic fill from pillows and even insulation. Just need something that is not going to foul your mix and can be pressure cooked.

Planttc sells little kits I liked a lot. Tcmultkit. Makes a liter, includes a preservative that is harder to come by. Keep at it, with a bit of practice you will get it down.

Didn't know you could over do the agar! Man this stuff is finicky. I've been getting my media from Caisson an trying a few different recipes from various white papers. Even though I am in a lab I'm lacking a good mg scale, and we just got a ph meter in. Te hormones I have are 2,4-D, IAA, and BA in powder but I'm reading conflicting things about adding them before/after autoclaving the media. Also my scale isn't getting accurate amounts I tried using 0.001g and keeping ratios the same with the hope that degradation from the autoclave would counteract the increased amount. Also thinking I didn't prep my plants right. One paper sounded like you could just plunk them on after they germinated and get callus induction, but I think I need to do root clippings or dissect the embryo out.

Well, I used planttc s kits and there is no measuring, just mix, put in jars, cook. Perfect every time. As for the degradation of hormone, it's a possibility, but I think that is accountedfor in recipes. I wouldn't add anything but plant after cooking, mixing destroys agar matrix, and you risk contamination.

A good mg scale is less than 15$ on amazon, worth it. I did some seeds straight in media after sanitizing, they do however root in the mult formulae due to seed hormones, simply cut the plantlet in half, discard the root section, if you have roots you get too much stretchy growth, and rooting stage is supposed to be later when you are readying plants to come out of TC.

If the plantlet falls down and the leaves touch the media, you will get weird growth, not ideal. The agar needs to be left alone after cooking undisturbed to set for 24 hrs. Make sure it comes out of the autoclave immediately and gets set In it's final location.

If you haven't practiced with jello shots, it's the same procedure, except you and your friends get to get drunk off jello shots, which in hindsight is how I met a lot of my college friends...

Once you have plantlet in culture multiplying and branching, it's a matter of cutting it up every so often in 5-100 pieces, kind of fun really. Iris's are a good learning plant, but any woody plant does good. Some soft tissue plants are harder.

How long does it normally take to observe callus formation?

Yay for gellification! Now what did you do differently?

Callus formation varies based on the type of plant, but a rough guess is 2 weeks.

Did you cut the root end off?

I did a quick test and made 125ml (x5) of CLC EP + 7g/l, 7.5g/l... Up to 9g/l Carrageenan. All gelled. Autoclaved at 250F/15min. Poured immediately. Doesn't really pin point anything but still good.

Yesterday I did CLC CP + 7g/l Carrageenan + 10um 2,4-D + 1um BA. Did the hormones through a stock solution/sterile syringe filter after autoclaving. That solved the scale issue and those plates all gelled too.

I removed the seed coat from the embryos and trimmed off the leaves and root caps. I threw them on the EP plates but am putting 1/2 them on the CP today since I'm not 100% sure how to use CLC media. I read to slice the embryo tips 1/2 lengthwise. So I am going to treat one that way and leave one unsliced to see if that it the way to go.

Much of doing tc experiments is numbers, maybe try to increase your test sample size to 5 of each method, sometimes for your more interesting experiments you may only have an early success rate in the 10-30% range and only doing one or two may give you false negatives.

I've never added hormone after autoclaving. It was all premixed and once they were cooked the trays were kept sealed until ready to use. I also did large batches of jars (the baby food jars with tc lids were better for me than plates due to the height of the plantlet I wanted) and kept a stack of 50-300 ready to go ones of different mixes depending on what I wanted to throw in there.

So what are you doing that you only want stem callus? Are you trying to generate and isolate a specific compound of the morning glory?

I want callus to et to the plant stem cells. Root or shoot cells doesn't matter much. Actually there's one paper that got them off a cambium core sample. Growing up some plants to try that as well. It's likely all just for fun, but plant stem cells are being used mainly in cosmetic applications. Since I work in a human cell lab I have a unique opportunity to do some co-culture and see if they have any valuable properties in increasing stem cell growth like some not so scholarly papers claim. A lot of those peepers focus on magic apple cells. I'm working with a close morning glory species that is also used in a stem cell stimulating supplement created by our lab owner. He isn't really aware of what I'm up to. It's like a personal curiosity that could lead to something we could turn into a product. At this point I'm just happy if my media gels. Lol! Didn't think it would be so challenging but I'm enjoying it!

Cool deal. It sounds like you are having fun with it, that's important.
